plan.hypothesis: H0: R² = 0 (all regression coefficients except intercept are zero); HA: R² > 0
assumptions: Predictor matrix is of full rank
Errors are normally distributed with constant variance (homoscedasticity)
Multiple correlation = 0.30 is the anticipated population effect size
scientific_notes: Test of overall model fit via F-statistic comparing full model (intercept + 3 predictors) against null (intercept only)
Noncentrality parameter λ = n × R² / (1 - R²) for the noncentral F distribution
Degrees of freedom: numerator = 3 (number of predictors), denominator = n - 4 = 76
Power is P(F > F_critical) under the noncentral F distribution with specified noncentrality

answer.summary: For a linear regression model with an intercept and 3 predictors tested against the null hypothesis H₀: R² = 0, with n = 80 participants, anticipated multiple correlation ρ = 0.30 (R² = 0.09), and significance level α = 0.05, the power to reject the null hypothesis using the noncentral F-test is 0.624 (approximately 62.4%).
answer.method: Noncentral F-test. The test statistic is F = [R²/(1-R²)] × [(n-p-1)/p], where R² = ρ² is the coefficient of determination, p = 3 is the number of predictors, and n = 80 is the sample size. This follows a noncentral F-distribution with numerator df = p = 3, denominator df = n - p - 1 = 76, and noncentrality parameter λ = n × R²/(1-R²) = 80 × 0.09/(1-0.09) ≈ 7.912. Power is calculated as P(F > F_critical) where F_critical = qf(1 - α, 3, 76) ≈ 2.725.
assumptions: Predictor matrix has full rank (no perfect multicollinearity)
Errors are normally distributed with constant variance (homoscedasticity)
Anticipated multiple correlation ρ = 0.30 represents the true population effect size
limitations: Power calculation assumes the anticipated multiple correlation of 0.30 is accurate; sensitivity should be checked if this value is uncertain
No finite-sample corrections beyond degrees-of-freedom adjustment are applied
The calculation assumes a one-sided test of R² > 0 (equivalent to testing whether the model explains significantly more variance than chance)

executions.code:
# Parameters
n <- 80                    # sample size (participants)
p <- 3                     # number of predictors (excluding intercept)
R_squared <- 0.30^2        # R-squared (coefficient of determination)
alpha <- 0.05              # significance level
rho <- 0.30                # multiple correlation (given)

# R-squared from multiple correlation
R_squared <- rho^2
cat("Multiple correlation (rho):", rho, "\n")
cat("R-squared:", R_squared, "\n")

# Degrees of freedom
df_num <- p                 # numerator df = number of predictors
df_denom <- n - p - 1      # denominator df = n - p - 1 (excluding intercept)
cat("Numerator df:", df_num, "\n")
cat("Denominator df:", df_denom, "\n")

# Critical F-value at alpha level
F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_num, df_denom)
cat("Critical F-value:", F_crit, "\n")

# Noncentrality parameter: lambda = n * R^2 / (1 - R^2)
lambda <- n * R_squared / (1 - R_squared)
cat("Noncentrality parameter (lambda):", lambda, "\n")

# Power: P(F > F_crit) under noncentral F(df_num, df_denom, lambda)
power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df_num, df_denom, lambda)
cat("Power:", power, "\n")

# Return result
result <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)

cat("\n=== RESULT ===\n")
print(result)

# Export as JSON
library(jsonlite)
output <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
  )
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", toJSON(output, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")
